transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well... my wife told me to come. She gets frustrated because she'll be talking to me about things... like my cousin's appointments or who's giving him rides... and I'm looking right at her. But then a minute later, I realize I didn't actually hear half of what she said. So... she wanted me to see someone.
Were you like this as a child, too?

I suppose. Um... yeah, even back in grade school. My teachers used to tell my parents I was bright, but... I guess I was always daydreaming. I'd leave my homework in my desk, or... they'd have to remind me to finish my classwork. That was before I was 12, I think. It's been a long time.
Have you always found it hard to understand other people’s social cues, like facial expressions or tone of voice?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I have a problem with that. I can usually tell if someone is upset or... you know. I just don't always catch the actual words they're saying.
Has your trouble paying attention been getting worse over the past year or so?
I suppose... yeah. It's been a bit more noticeable lately. Maybe for the last 11 months or so. Um... my cousin moved in with us after he had surgery. So... it's just been harder since then, I guess.
Have you had any head injury or other medical event around the time your attention got worse?
No. Nothing like that. Just... regular life stuff, I guess.
